product: Uranium concentrate (U3O8) and fuel services including UF6 and UO2 conversion and heavy-water reactor fuel bundles, plus equity interests in Westinghouse and Global Laser Enrichment and purchased pounds from JV Inkai in Kazakhstan.
demand: Demand is rising as governments and utilities expand nuclear capacity for energy security and decarbonization, and long-term contracting picked up in the first half of 2026; consensus still models roughly flat 2026 revenue near CAD 3.49B with growth in 2027.
pricing_power: Strong and improving. Market-related contracts are resetting realized prices higher in uranium and fuel services and management is deliberately withholding supply to capture future upside, though the existing long-term book caps near-term gains.
competition: In uranium: Kazatomprom, Orano, CGN and other producers plus secondary supply. In reactors and the fuel cycle: Westinghouse competes with EDF, Rosatom, GE-Hitachi and Korean and Chinese vendors.
team: CEO Tim Gitzel and President and COO Grant Isaac lead; Catherine Gignac chairs the board. Director Dominique Miniere stepped down effective Jul 26 2026. A United Steelworkers Local 8914 agreement at Key Lake and McArthur River runs to December 2028.
market_strategy: Sell directly to utilities under long-term, market-related contracts while staying patient and selective on new commitments, own scarce tier-one assets such as the enlarged Cigar Lake stake, buy pounds in the spot market when cheap, and invest across the fuel cycle including Westinghouse.
bull: Long-term contracting and market-related resets lift realized uranium and fuel-services prices; over 28 Mlb/yr committed for five years, tier-one Cigar Lake stake enlarged, and 2026 production guidance unchanged despite outages.
bear: Q2 2026 net earnings only $25M with Westinghouse at a $10M share loss; deliveries lower by design; Barclays cut to $97 Hold Aug 4 2026; 63-day momentum -0.1293; consensus models flat 2026 revenue.
falsifier: Cameco's Q3 2026 report on Nov 3-4 2026 shows another production or delivery cut, or Westinghouse equity earnings still negative, versus unchanged 2026 guidance of 19.5-21.5 Mlb.
web_what_changed: Last 90 days: Jul 31 2026 Q2 results showed net earnings of only $25M and much lower Westinghouse equity earnings; Jul 1 Cigar Lake was suspended and Jul 14 resumed after trouble at Orano's McClean Lake mill; Jun 1 Cameco agreed to buy TEPCO's 5% Cigar Lake interest; May 27 McArthur River and Key Lake resumed after flooding; 2026 production guidance unchanged.
web_not_known_yesterday: Nothing material is newly known as of 2026-09-25. Cameco has issued no news release since the Jul 31 2026 Q2 report, the engine records zero news items in 30 days, and the IR events page would not load, so today's known state is essentially unchanged from the prior day.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is price, not volume. Management says average realized prices keep improving in uranium and fuel services as market-related contracts reset higher, while 2026 sales deliveries are deliberately lower under contracting discipline (Q2 deliveries 7.1 Mlb). So price and mix, not volume.
web_suppliers: Key suppliers are Orano, which processes Cigar Lake ore at the McClean Lake mill, and JV Inkai in Kazakhstan (4.2 Mlb purchase allocation for 2026). Yes, constrained: an acid-plant problem at McClean Lake halted Cigar Lake in July 2026, with sulfuric acid sourcing and northern Saskatchewan road access as bottlenecks.
web_customers: Utilities in 16 countries: about 39 U3O8 customers and 33 UF6 conversion customers, with roughly 220 Mlb U3O8 and 85 Mkg UF6 contracted and over 28 Mlb per year committed for the next five years. Concentrated among large state-owned and private nuclear utilities.
web_who_loses: Rival uranium producers and holders of secondary supply (Kazatomprom, Orano, ROSATOM-linked units, CGN) lose pricing leverage; conversion and enrichment sellers face costlier feed; spot buyers and traders lose cheap pounds; gas, coal and renewables lose share as nuclear is prioritized for energy security.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 net earnings fell to $25M and Westinghouse swung to a $10M share loss; deliveries are lower by design; Barclays cut its target to $97 with a Hold on Aug 4 2026; flooding and mill outages show execution risk; consensus models roughly flat 2026 revenue (about CAD 3.49B); the engine flags negative 63-day momentum of -0.1293.
web_if_management_right: A stronger long-term uranium price plus Westinghouse's pipeline of up to 91 AP1000 opportunities, US DOE conditional AP1000 support and Canada's June 2026 Nuclear Energy Strategy lift realized prices, sustain over 28 Mlb yearly contracted deliveries, restore Westinghouse equity earnings and deliver 19.5-21.5 Mlb of 2026 share production.
web_if_management_wrong: Supply execution breaks first. Another Cigar Lake, McClean Lake or Key Lake outage from sulfuric acid, flooding or road access cuts 2026 production and deliveries, while slow AP1000 order conversion keeps Westinghouse equity earnings negative, pressuring cash flow and the premium valuation.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Uranium developers and peers such as Kazatomprom, Denison, NexGen and Uranium Energy; physical uranium holders and royalty companies; conversion and enrichment providers such as Centrus and Urenco; nuclear equipment and EPC suppliers; SMR developers; Saskatchewan service and logistics firms.
